implementation_notes: Rust's answer is a conditional layer: ServiceBuilder::option_layer(Some(AuditLayer::new()) if enabled else None) wraps the inner service in Either<Audit, Identity>, so the switched-off stack contains no branch at all while the request still reaches the same inner service - the bypass leg is literally the identity layer. Layer order is the route definition, which is why tower documents that layers added first are called first. For a toggle that must flip without a restart, keep the layer installed and read an AtomicBool (or tower::filter) inside it.
pitfalls: option_layer requires both wrapped services to share Request/Response/Error types; mixed types need BoxService/BoxCloneService.
A toggle resolved at construction means a restart to flip it - keep the layer and check an AtomicBool inside for a live switch.
Wrapping a cloneable service with stateful layers (buffers, limits, replay logs) changes clone semantics; a shared detour buffer must be Arc-shared deliberately.
